chunk_findings.detail: `_delta` computes the changed-path delta with `git diff --name-only`, which under default Git rename detection reports only the destination path for a rename. That can omit the old source path from the delta, so tests that still import the old module are not considered reached. Example: a full pass is recorded on commit A containing `src/mod.py` and `tests/test_mod.py` importing `src.mod`. Commit B renames `src/mod.py` to `src/new_mod.py` but does not touch `tests/test_mod.py`. `git diff --name-only A B` returns only `src/new_mod.py`; `_delta` returns that path; the selector sees no test importing `new_mod` and may return no tests/cut/unparsed; `assess` then returns `STANDS` with outcome `"passed"`. Running the suite on B fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src.mod'`, so the pass wrongly stands. If the renamed destination is filtered as a doc or state path, the delta can become empty even though the old source was deleted. The delta should include both sides of renames, e.g. by using `--no-renames` or parsing `--name-status`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/revalidate.py `_delta` (`G.paths(repo, "diff", "--name-only", a, b)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The help states that changed paths are stripped of `.ddflow/` and “documents” *before* they are looked up in the test closure, so a change that only touches a document can be classified as “None reached” and preserve the old full-suite pass. Given a repo where a document is a test input—e.g. `docs/parallel.md` is read by `tests/test_parallel_help.py`—a main move whose only changed path is that document is removed from the delta before closure lookup, `revalidate.assess` returns `unchanged by delta`, and the phase closes on the stale pass even though the change did reach a test. Either the documented policy is wrong, or the implementation described by it wrongly preserves passes for document changes that affect tests.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md (added section, lines ~128-133)

chunk_findings.detail: The clean-selector assertion treats a delta that reaches a test as a passed combination even though the selected test is known to fail and no successful test run has been recorded. The test first commits `pkg/a.py` to return `9` (line 121), while the selected `tests/test_a.py` created earlier asserts `a.f() == 1`. The `clean` selector returns only that selected test, and line 129 asserts `assess(repo, a, b, selector=clean).outcome == "passed"`. If `RV.assess` is used to decide whether the prior full-suite pass stands, this is exactly the wrong outcome: a delta that reaches a test must not be judged `passed` without running it. If `assess` does run the selected tests, the assertion is false because the selected test fails; if it does not run them, the verdict fabricates a passing result for a test-reaching delta.

chunk_findings.detail: Once `_stands()` records a stand pass, that pass has a timestamp newer than the phase's last merge, so every later `missing()` call returns `""` at the early `passed > merged` check before the delta hook is consulted. The delta from the stand pass's recorded SHA to the current HEAD is therefore never re-assessed. Example: a phase's last merge is at `T0`; an old pass at `T0-1` records SHA `A`; main moves to `B` with no test changes, so `_stands` appends a pass at `B` with timestamp `T1 > T0`; main then moves to `C` where a test file (or code reachable by tests) changed, but no new phase merge event occurs. The next `missing()` sees `passed=T1 > merged=T0` and returns `""`, bypassing the `B..C` delta and allowing a phase to complete as fully passed even though the suite may fail on `C`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/phase_suite.py:missing (stand recording path)

chunk_findings.detail: The added rule subtracts “`.ddflow/` and documents” from the delta *before* the test-closure lookup. If a changed document is itself a test input, the path is discarded before assess can see that a test depends on it. Concrete input: main moves by editing a Markdown file that a test/snapshot reads and asserts on (for example, this help prompt or another `.md` fixture); `revalidate.assess` removes it as a “document”, sees no delta reached in the closure, returns `unchanged by delta`, and `ddflow complete` keeps the old full-suite pass even though the test would fail on the new main. The document/`.ddflow/` exclusion must be applied only after determining the path is not in the test closure, or limited to files known never to be test inputs.

chunk_findings.detail: The clean-selector assertion expects `assess(...).outcome == "passed"` for a delta that reaches `tests/test_a.py` and changes `pkg/a.py` to `return 9`, while the only test in the repository asserts `a.f() == 1`. Given the initial pass at `a`, this input is a known failing delta: the selected test cannot pass. If `Verdict.outcome == "passed"` is used anywhere to keep or close a pass (as the true-stand assertion at line 79 does), this test encodes a wrong pass; the clean selection should not be reported as passed before the selected failing test is actually run.
